note: From OpenStreetMap's main API (13 October 2026), 1.25 times real across the line like the tracks: two side platforms of about 108 m on the Buxton line, 2.1 m outside its two tracks (trains stop 24 m south of the station's point, so a two-car unit stands on them as they are and a six-car one once they're extended south, the north end being Albion Road's bridge), a lattice footbridge between them, Albion Road (the A6015) over the line at the west end, the car park and a white flat-roofed building on the north side. Positive v is north. The halt's platform (towards Manchester) is the south one, below the cutting's wall and Newtown Primary School, reached by a path up to Albion Road at its north end. Views from above (docs/reference/aerial/new-mills-newtown.jpg). Photos (docs/reference/photos/new-mills-newtown: geograph 8142971 and 8001487, 8001482, 8001479 JThomas 2025, 8280273 Stephen Craven 2026, 8402852, 8403230, 8403231, 8402851 and 8403234 DS Pugh 2026, 7688195 Stephen McKay 2024, 4311399 Roger D Kidd 2014): a green diamond-lattice footbridge with stairs down along each platform; a white flat-roofed building and a glazed shelter on the north platform; Albion Road's bridge with stone abutments and a steel deck with a red and white parapet band (drawn steel). The footbridge drawn as the lattice part (Ardwick's), its stairs' direction from OpenStreetMap's steps. The halt's shelter, canopy, kiosk, barriers, lifts and extension are the game's; the retaining wall's height from the LIDAR (the school stands about 9 m over the rails).
